result.title: When and How Order-Flow Interventions Work After Dealers Adapt
result.summary: Learning dealer agents can settle on persistently wide quotes, raising what customers pay to trade. A venue can route more orders to tighter quotes, but a wide quote may reflect real risk, and once dealers adapt, an end-to-end comparison cannot show why a rule works: because it intervenes more, picks better moments, is announced in advance, or rewards the right quote. We propose SOFA (State-aligned Order-Flow Allocation), a public order-flow contract with three parts: a State Scorer ranks market states from lagged public data, a Commitment Scheduler announces a budgeted intervention strength before dealers quote, and a Quote-to-Flow Allocator shifts a bounded share of fixed customer demand toward tighter quotes. Our paired re-adaptation protocol gives competing rules the same intervention strengths, only re-timed, lets dealers re-adapt to each rule from a shared checkpoint, and breaks one link at a time. Across 20 independently trained dealer populations in an ABIDES market, concentrating the intervention in states that the score ranks as low-risk lowers low-risk execution cost relative to random timing in every population, by 0.040 tick on average, while a stale announcement or a broken quote-to-flow link raises this cost. In the primary setting the gain comes at the expense of high-risk trades, whose costs rise, so state alignment pays off only for a venue that weighs low-risk costs more than 1.38 times as heavily as high-risk costs. Our code is available at https://github.com/moderncavemann/state-aligned-order-flow-contracts.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究做市商自适应后订单流干预何时以及为何有效，提出 SOFA 合约，由 State Scorer 从滞后公开数据给市场状态打分、Commitment Scheduler 在报价前预先公布干预强度、Quote-to-Flow Allocator 把固定客户需求的一部分导向更紧报价，并用配对再适应协议在 ABIDES 市场中逐条切断组件来归因。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「配对再适应、一次只切断一个环节、并让竞争规则共享同一干预强度」的因果归因设计，可能可供核查 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 等机制贡献分配与计算预算对照实验的评估方法，但领域距离较远，属推测性迁移线索。
